## Overview

This model uses a Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) to estimate a smooth association between receptive vocabulary and word reading. The curve allows the slope to vary across the observed exposure range. It is a nonlinear companion to [MECH-056](../lrp-rli-mech-056/), which estimates a single slope.

The declared sampling target is `target_accept=0.999`. A high target can help sampling, but it does not guarantee convergence or validate a curve. Read the diagnostics for the current fit rather than carrying earlier run results into this report.

**Sampling limit.** If the fit diverges, withhold the curve and its shape summaries. A sampling failure does not show that the association is linear or that no change in slope exists. Read the current publication decision before interpreting the curve.

## Adjustment set

Revised DAG (2026-07-10), re-derived by a backdoor d-separation search with the latent general ability ($GA$) held — the criterion that reproduces LRP56/58 and dose-077 exactly. $R$'s measured common causes of the exposure and word reading are $\{A, HS, TR, RW\}$; group $G\,(= IG)$ is the always-in precision term and $W_{\text{pre}}$ the autoregressive baseline. This is **identical to LRP56** — only the mechanism's functional form (nonparametric curve vs single slope) changes.

_Adjusted association, not causal._ Residual confounding by latent general ability ($GA$) remains, so $f^R$ is an **adjusted association**, not a causal effect. The corresponding randomised-arm result is an available-case modified ITT estimate in the ITT suite.
